import { gzipSync } from 'node:zlib';
const file = process.argv[2] ?? 'src/module.ts';
const r = await build({ entryPoints: [file], bundle: true, minify: true, treeShaking: true,
  format: 'esm', platform: 'browser', target: 'es2022', write: false, metafile: true, logLevel: 'silent' });
const own = Object.entries(Object.values(r.metafile.outputs)[0].inputs)
  .filter(([path]) => !path.includes('node_modules/'))
  .reduce((sum, [, info]) => sum + info.bytesInOutput, 0);
console.log(file, gzipSync(r.outputFiles[0].contents, { level: 9 }).byteLength, 'bytes (min+gzip),', own, 'bytes of own code');

The migrated file is at `out/module.ts`. It type-checks with no errors in `out/`, and `npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 2009 bytes (min+gzip) with 85 bytes of own code.

I couldn't compare against the original directly, because lodash isn't installed and I was told not to install anything. The behaviour claims below come from running es-toolkit and from what I know of lodash.

- **`applyPatch`**: uses `merge` from `es-toolkit`. Like lodash's `merge`, it mutates and returns `base`, merges arrays index by index, and assigns `null` from the patch. I checked those cases on sample inputs.
- **`toTitle`**: uses `startCase` from `es-toolkit/compat`. The main `es-toolkit` `startCase` lowercases the rest of each word, so `"USERName"` gives `"User Name"` where lodash gives `"USER Name"`. It also turns `"1st item"` into `"1 St Item"`. The compat version matches lodash on the inputs I tried.
- **`toLookup`**: uses `fromPairs` from `es-toolkit/compat`, since the main package has no `fromPairs`. For duplicate names the last pair wins, as in lodash.

Importing `merge` from compat as well came to 3669 bytes, so I kept the main-package `merge`.

No lodash imports remain, and I didn't hand-write any replacements.
